rows.note: Use 唔該 as the all-purpose colloquial polite request marker.

example.english: Please help me open the door.
example.jyutping: m4 goi1 nei5 bong1 ngo5 hoi1 mun4

rows.note: Use 請 before a request when a more formal or ceremonious tone is appropriate.

example.jyutping: cing2 gok3 wai2 bou2 ci4 on1 zing6

rows.note: This is the all-purpose choice when something makes a person happy or gives them pleasure.

example.english: This gift really does please me.
example.jyutping: ni1 fan6 lai5 mat6 ling6 ngo5 hou2 hoi1 sam1

rows.note: Use this when “please” means satisfy someone’s expectations or leave them satisfied.

example.english: This answer should please the client.
example.jyutping: ni1 go3 daap3 on3 ling6 haak3 jan4 mun5 ji3

rows.note: Use this when someone deliberately says or does something to cheer another person up or keep them happy.

example.english: They often tell jokes to please people.
example.traditional: 佢成日講笑話氹人開心。
example.jyutping: keoi5 seng4 jat6 gong2 siu3 waa6 tam2 jan4 hoi1 sam1

rows.note: Use this formal or written verb for pleasing or delighting a person, especially in more polished prose.

example.english: This arrangement successfully manages to please the guests.
example.traditional: 呢項安排成功取悅賓客。
example.jyutping: ni1 hong6 on1 paai4 sing4 gung1 ceoi2 jyut6 ban1 haak3
